styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: MASP, Ibirapuera and the historic Centro.

styles.label: Nightlife
styles.blurb: Bars in Vila Madalena and live samba.

stays.why: Leafy, safe and central. Walk to Avenida Paulista and the MASP; good restaurants nearby.
Right on the main avenue and metro line. Best base for first-time sightseeing.
Street art, bars and nightlife. Livelier and a bit rougher; use ride apps at night.
Cheapest and closest to historic sights and markets. Busy by day, quiet after dark; check the block.

food: Try a Brazilian lunch: feijoada (bean and pork stew) or a prato feito (rice, beans, meat and salad), often R$30–60.
Mercado Municipal downtown: pastel de bacalhau and huge mortadella sandwiches. Go before noon to beat the crowds.
Padarias (bakeries) serve cheap breakfasts and coffee all day; a pão na chapa and coffee is about R$10–15.
São Paulo has strong Japanese, Italian and Arab food. Look for restaurants in Liberdade and Bixiga.
Churrascarias and kilo buffets (comida por kilo) are good value; pay by weight, usually R$60–100 per kilo.
more_time: Add a day for Ibirapuera Park and the museums around it; it is a big park and easy to spend half a day.
Swap one city day for a trip to the coast or the hills; check bus times and prices on the day.
Art lovers can swap a shopping afternoon for the Pinacoteca and the Luz area near the Centro.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the main museums, the Centro and a night out, with time for long meals.

month_notes: Jan: hot and very wet, about 24 rain days. Pack a rain jacket and plan indoor backups.
Feb: hot and still wet, around 19 rain days. Mornings are often the driest window.
Mar: warm with about 19 rain days. Short heavy afternoon showers are common.
Apr: milder and drier, about 10 rain days. Good month for walking the city.
May: cooler days around 23°C and only 8 rain days. Bring a light jacket for evenings.
Jun: cool and dry, about 6 rain days. Mornings can be chilly at around 13°C.
Jul: the driest month, about 3 rain days. Cool nights near 12°C; pack a warm layer.
Aug: dry and mild, about 6 rain days. Comfortable days for parks and long walks.
Sep: warming up with about 8 rain days. Pleasant before the spring rains.
Oct: warmer and wetter, about 15 rain days. Carry a small umbrella.
Nov: warm with about 17 rain days. Showers return; plan flexible afternoons.
Dec: hot and wet, about 21 rain days. Expect holiday crowds and afternoon storms.

climate_guide.summary: Subtropical and mild year-round, with a dry, cool winter (Jun–Aug) and a wet, warm summer (Dec–Mar).

items.title: Best time: April to September
items.text: Milder days around 22–26°C and fewer rain days. July is the driest, with about 3 rain days.

items.title: Summer is wet (Dec–Mar)
items.text: About 19–24 rain days a month. Storms are often short and heavy; keep indoor plans ready.

items.title: Winter nights are cool
items.text: June to August lows sit around 12–13°C. Days stay mild near 22°C. Bring a jacket.

items.title: Carry an umbrella in summer
items.text: Downpours come fast from December to March. A small umbrella beats waiting it out.

items.title: No extreme heat
items.text: Highs stay around 22–27°C all year. It is rarely very hot or very cold.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, a rain jacket or umbrella, comfy walking shoes and a warm layer for winter evenings.

transit.best: Metrô for long hops; Uber or 99 for late nights and hilly areas.

modes.text: Modern, safe and the fastest way around. Lines 1–5 and 9 suit tourists.
Covers the whole city. Fares are R$5.30; Bilhete Único gives free transfers within 3 hours.
Taxis are metered; Guarucoop has a monopoly at GRU and fares are posted. Uber and 99 are widely used and usually cheaper.
Driving is stressful. Traffic peaks 06:00–09:00 and 16:00–19:00, so avoid renting a car.
Fine in central and Jardins areas. Bikes are popular too, with many cycleways.
CPTM trains are modern and safe; Line 9 is useful for tourists.
